brief:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's interim administration can legally launch military operations against Iran despite serving in a caretaker capacity, Al Jazeera English reported. Israeli law permits a caretaker government to wage war, though such action would likely deepen domestic divisions within the country.

The question of whether Netanyahu might order an attack before leaving office remains open, with the legal framework presenting no formal obstacle to military strikes.
dek: PM's caretaker government can legally go to war, though it would likely inflame domestic divisions.
title: Netanyahu's caretaker government retains legal authority to strike Iran
